label: D2 after choosing a1, early in the episode (first ~30 trials)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass), and only when this trial's GO choice was a1 (in_action == 1 at D2, observed). It is also gated by episode time: rate is ~13% in trials 0-19, falls in 20-39, and is zero from trial 40 on. With D2 & a1 & ep_trial < 30 the dev scores are P 0.71, R 0.95, F1 0.81, mass recall 0.98. Cutoffs of 27 or 35 trade precision against recall. Never fires at D1/GO, after a2 choices, or late in the episode. It fires on both reached states. The top-activating windows are dominated by rare a1->S2 transitions in runs of repeated a1 choices, but S1 common steps also fire. Higher rates when S1 is good or the episode started S1-good are correlates of choosing a1. All variables used are observed at D2; ep_trial is elapsed time, not a hidden variable.

issues: The main factual claims hold. On dev, D1 and GO each have 0 active steps out of 380619. All firing is at in_action==1, with zero at in_action==2. 99.98% of the mass is at ep_trial<40. It fires whichever state is reached: S1 holds 69% of the mass and S2 31%. The test scores reproduce (P 0.698, R 0.948, F1 0.804, MR 0.983).

Systematic false-positive class the explanation does not mention: when this trial's a1 is a switch from a2 (prev_action==2), the feature barely fires. Within the predicate this class has P 0.269 on dev and 0.239 on test, and holds only 1.7% of the mass. The profile shows the same thing: the firing rate is 0.064 when prev_action==1 and 0.002 when prev_action==2. So the feature is about D2 on repeated a1 choices, not any a1 choice.

The cutoff at 30 overclaims the time gate. Within the predicate, precision is 0.85 for trials 0-19 but 0.474 for trials 20-29 (dev and test), and that band holds only 14% of the mass. Firing fades out gradually rather than having a hard edge, and most false positives come from trials 20-29. The explanation's own note that a cutoff of 27 gives a higher F1 points the same way.

The claim that the S1-good / start_high effects are only a side effect of choosing a1 more is partly wrong. Even after conditioning on D2 & a1 & ep_trial<30, precision is 0.757 when start_high==1 and 0.521 when start_high==0, and 86% of the mass is in start_high==1 episodes. The good-state effect, by contrast, is mostly explained by the a1 base rate: within the predicate, P is 0.70 when good==1 and 0.64 when good==2.

Smaller points: the very first trials (ep_trial<2) almost never fire (P 0.27, mass ~0), and precision rises with the policy's preference for a1 (P 0.93 when choice>2.78, 0.33 when choice<-1.52). Within these windows, activation also tends to decay over long runs of rewarded common a1->S1 trials.

Better predicate: (phase == D2) & (action == 1) & (ep_trial < 25) & (prev_action != 2). Dev: P 0.840, R 0.842, F1 0.841. Test: P 0.839, R 0.840, F1 0.839, MR 0.918, compared with 0.804 for the original. It uses only variables observed at D2.
